digest.component_or_area: completion verification gate with pinned read-only ticket store view
propositions: Full ticket-store materialization takes 135–235 seconds for 5,500 directories and 132,000 files; a scoped pinned-OID read using Git plumbing and lazy object loads completes in ~29 ms, roughly 4,600–8,000 times faster

Pinned Git tree reads at a captured commit OID remain byte-identical even after concurrent live mutations advance HEAD, enabling stable completion verification while close/sidecar/signature operations continue

Validation must track exact ticket reads, predicate matches (direct children, transitive descendants, relation membership), and global resolver inputs (e.g. .bridge_state/bindings.json); unrelated ticket mutations leave dependencies valid while structural changes invalidate them
Isolated scoped-ticket reduction retains unresolved alias links because resolver context is missing; full-store reduction resolves them—this asymmetry is a design gotcha for lazy pinned views

Completion sidecars must atomically combine COMPLETION_VERDICT + closing STATUS + SIGNATURE in a single local Git commit under a short lock, then publish via fast-forward CAS; interim PASS sidecars or unsigned STATUS must be rejected

Parallel completion reviews must detect and retry on HEAD conflicts by revalidating changed ticket directories and hierarchies; cache collisions on shared per-criterion temp paths and live-code mixing with pinned-code inputs are separate blocking bugs
